title: Minimax Rates for Treated Effects When the Valid Donor Switches with a Continuous Covariate
banked_reason: D0.5.G cold tier: incremental; paper_score_ceiling 6.1 < field threshold 7.4; meets_floor=false; salvageable=false.

proof_attempt_summary: The run proved matching plug-in upper bounds, compatible switching and full-class root-n phases, and two nonnested one-dimensional nonregular families using explicit Bernoulli switching witnesses. The promised all-regime frontier did not close: in higher-dimensional or weaker-margin regimes the single-bump lower constructions do not match the upper exponent, and the joint-noise obstruction has no matching higher-order estimator or honest interval. Completing it requires new multibump or moment-matched approximation theory rather than a bounded repair of the present derivation.
tldr: When the exactly valid donor changes with a continuous covariate, the panel ATT is identified but its identifying functional is nonsmooth in noisy pre-validity and post-payoff axes. On the full base class, every fixed binary-prepath regime satisfying the elementary constant-law membership conditions has minimax risk and uniformly honest expected length of order \(n^{-1/2}\) whenever \(\beta(\rho+\kappa)/(2\beta+d)\geq1/2\), for every \(\kappa>0\) and without any switching-feasibility premise. A separate radial-bump theorem retains the stronger root-\(n\) conclusion for a genuine-switching subclass under its compatibility conditions. Two nonnested sufficient one-dimensional constructions give matching possibly nonregular frontiers, and a compatible high-dimensional joint-noise construction gives an \(n^{-4/(d+5)}\) lower obstruction when \(\beta=\rho=\kappa=1\) and \(d>3\). The nonregular full-class phase, fixed constants outside the sufficient collections, the matching joint-noise frontier, and simultaneous honest-to-oracle adaptation remain open.
gap: The closest causal paper permits a covariate-dependent valid comparison set and explicitly leaves continuous-covariate estimation for future work. Existing margin, optimal-value, and nonsmooth-functional results do not determine the rate for a selector driven by one smooth pre-period signal with loss transmitted through a separately observed post-period signal, nor the uniformly honest confidence length in the full panel experiment.
fill: Establish matching upper and lower rates on every nonempty switching regime, locate root-n and logarithmic elbows, construct an honest interval at the sharp length, prove or refute simultaneous oracle adaptation, and validate every lower bound inside actual potential-outcome panel laws.
